tooltip.title: CTCL Treatment Overview
tooltip.markdown: Treatment is stage-adapted, prioritizing immune-preserving, skin-directed therapies for early disease and escalating to systemic agents for advanced or refractory cases. The goal is long-term disease control and palliation, not cure.

tooltip.title: Skin-Directed Therapies (SDT)
tooltip.markdown: Cornerstone of treatment for early-stage MF (IA-IIA). Can be used as adjunctive therapy at any stage to control skin-based symptoms.

tooltip.title: Topical Corticosteroids
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Mechanism:** Anti-inflammatory, antimitotic, and immunosuppressive.
-   **Use:** Preferred first-line option for Stage IA MF; adjunctive use for pruritus at all stages.
-   **Side Effects:** Skin atrophy, striae, potential for adrenal suppression with widespread use of high-potency agents.

tooltip.title: Topical Mechlorethamine (Nitrogen Mustard)
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Mechanism:** Topical alkylating agent (chemotherapy).
-   **Use:** First- or second-line for Stage IA/IB MF.
-   **Side Effects:** High rate of irritant or allergic contact dermatitis; hypo/hyperpigmentation.

tooltip.title: Phototherapy
tooltip.markdown: Used for generalized patch or plaque disease.

tooltip.title: Narrowband UVB (NB-UVB)
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Use:** Effective for patch-stage disease (T1a/T2a).
-   **Considerations:** Less deep penetration than PUVA.

tooltip.title: Psoralen + UVA (PUVA)
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Use:** Deeper penetration makes it effective for thicker plaques (T1b/T2b).
-   **Side Effects:** Higher risk of non-melanoma skin cancer than UVB.

tooltip.title: Radiation Therapy
tooltip.markdown: Highly effective for clearing localized lesions.

tooltip.title: Localized Superficial Radiation
tooltip.markdown: Excellent for treating a single persistent plaque or tumor.

tooltip.title: Total Skin Electron Beam
tooltip.markdown: Used for widespread, refractory plaque disease or erythrodermic MF.

tooltip.title: Systemic Therapies
tooltip.markdown: Used for advanced-stage disease (IIB-IV), refractory early-stage disease, or Sézary Syndrome.

tooltip.title: Oral Retinoids
tooltip.markdown: Bexarotene is FDA-approved for CTCL. Acitretin is used off-label. Often combined with other therapies like phototherapy or IFN-α.

tooltip.title: Interferon-alfa (IFN-α)
tooltip.markdown: An immunomodulatory agent, often used in combination with other therapies.

tooltip.title: Histone Deacetylase (HDAC) Inhibitors
tooltip.markdown: Romidepsin and Vorinostat are FDA-approved for relapsed/refractory CTCL.

tooltip.title: Systemic Chemotherapy
tooltip.markdown: Reserved for advanced, refractory, or transformed disease due to toxicity and short duration of response. Includes single-agent (e.g., Gemcitabine, Doxil) and multi-agent regimens.

tooltip.title: Targeted Biologic Agents
tooltip.markdown: Modern therapies that target specific molecules on the malignant T-cells.

tooltip.title: Brentuximab Vedotin (Anti-CD30)
tooltip.markdown: An antibody-drug conjugate targeting CD30. Highly effective for CD30+ LPDs and transformed MF.

tooltip.title: Mogamulizumab (Anti-CCR4)
tooltip.markdown: A monoclonal antibody targeting CCR4. FDA-approved for relapsed/refractory MF/SS.

tooltip.title: Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP)
tooltip.markdown: A first-line therapy for Sézary Syndrome. Involves treating the patient's white blood cells with a photosensitizer and UVA light outside the body.
